docs.creator: Marks, Leo
description: 613 pages, 8 unnumbered pages of plates : 25 cm

"Leo Marks was head of the code department of SOE during the Second World War and his tender and tormented memoir, Between Silk and Cyanide - which has taken him more than eight years to write - gives a unique picture of this extraordinary organization at work and discloses for the first time many truths about SOE and the conduct of the war." "SOE (Special Operations Executive) was created in July 1940 with a mandate from Churchill to 'Set Europe Ablaze'. Its main function was to infiltrate agents into enemy-occupied territory to perform acts of sabotage and form Secret Armies. Leo Marks joined SOE in 1942. He was twenty-two. A cryptographer of genius, he revolutionized the concept of agents' codes by the time he was twenty-three, devising and implementing a system of printing codes on silk - to be camouflaged as handkerchiefs, underwear, or coat linings - which could be destroyed message by message, and couldn't possibly be remembered." "Of all his revelations none is more astonishing than his account of the code war between SOE and the Germans in Holland, which has never previously been disclosed. He also reveals for the first time how SOE fooled the Germans into thinking that a Secret Army was operating in the Fatherland itself, and how and why he broke General de Gaulle's secret code."--Jacket
docs.title: Between silk and cyanide : the story of SOE's code war
